headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Plandex can write/modify code while ctx observes Claude Code events and filesystem content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx ingests Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and has filesystem access, while Plandex reads/writes the project directory and can auto-apply changes. If Plandex or ctx processes attacker-controlled file content as instructions, a shared workspace can bridge injection. The pathway is plausible in default use, though not directly documented for this exact pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or shared workspace
IF ctx parses file or event content as trusted instructions
IF Plandex auto-applies changes without human review
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Restrict ctx to read-only observation
Add provenance tags to shared files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, harness records, graph data, and MCP servers; Plandex reads the filesystem and sends context to a model provider or Plandex Cloud/self-hosted server. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from ctx-observed files into Plandex uploads or model prompts. This is a default-configuration risk, not a proven exfiltration event.
conditions: IF ctx writes logs or graph data into the shared project directory
IF Plandex ingests those files into its plan context
IF Plandex is configured to use a remote model provider or cloud backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive logs outside the shared directory
Use separate OS users or containers
Disable remote model backends for sensitive projects
Review file inclusion lists before planning
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, while Plandex can execute shell, modify git state, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Both can mutate the same codebase, and Plandex explicitly supports shared state via a backend. Without locking or coordination, concurrent writes and git changes can collide and corrupt work.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory
IF ctx or Plandex performs writes concurrently
IF git operations occur without external locking
mitigations: Serialize writes through one operator
Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent during git operations
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file and git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and Plandex uses review-then-apply or optional auto-apply. If ctx-generated context or Plandex plans are treated as authoritative, one agent's output can become the other's action trigger without verification. That creates a realistic path from mistaken analysis to incorrect code changes or commands.
conditions: IF ctx-derived summaries are used as authoritative inputs
IF no human review occurs before shell or file actions
mitigations: Keep Plandex in review-only mode
Require human approval for apply steps
Cross-check ctx outputs against source files
Limit ctx to advisory logging
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show a specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only concrete compliance-relevant data classes are ctx's logs/records and Plandex's source code and model-provider keys, so the pair suggests policy-management work rather than a documented breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined handling of data classes.
conditions: IF audit/runtime logs contain regulated data
IF those logs are sent to a remote model provider
IF retention policies differ between the two tools
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of logs
Use a local/self-hosted backend
Set explicit retention limits
Review secret-handling settings
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
